entries.title: Critical alerts get buried under low-severity noise in the alert queue
entries.statement: The alert queue carries high volume with few relevant alerts, and critical alerts on important assets end up below large numbers of low-severity alerts. In one case a critical alert waited 40 minutes at night.

evidence.quote: Honestly the queue is the pain. On a bad day we get two, three hundred alerts and maybe ten matter.
A low on a test box should never be above a critical on a domain controller.
A critical alert on our file server sat in the queue for 40 minutes on the night shift.
It was below 60 low alerts from a scanner.

entries.title: Sort the alert queue by danger, not arrival time
entries.statement: Customers want the queue to show the most dangerous alerts first, based on severity and the affected asset, rather than ordered by time.

evidence.quote: For me, show me what's dangerous first. Sort by what it hits, not when it came in.
Can the queue show critical first?

entries.title: Show whether the affected asset is test or production
entries.statement: Analysts want an asset column indicating whether the affected machine is test or production, as the first thing they check.

evidence.quote: I need to know if it's a test box or production before anything else.

entries.title: Analysts scan the queue by time and overlook severity
entries.statement: In usability testing, 4 of 5 analysts scanned the queue top to bottom by time (median 74 seconds to find the critical alert) and 3 of 5 did not look at the Severity column until prompted.

evidence.quote: 4 of 5 scanned the queue top to bottom by time. Median 74 seconds to find the critical alert.
3 of 5 did not look at the Severity column at all until prompted.

entries.title: Severity column is visually indistinguishable
entries.statement: The Severity column reads as uniform grey text, so analysts don't notice it.

evidence.quote: Oh, there's a severity column? It's all the same grey text.

entries.title: Duplicate PowerShell alerts from test/CI runners flood the queue
entries.statement: The same PowerShell alert from test or CI runners fires dozens of times a day, creating noise in the alert queue.

evidence.quote: The duplicate PowerShell thing from test runners is also noisy
We get the same PowerShell alert from our CI runners dozens of times a day.

entries.title: Analysts waste time on, or learn to ignore, duplicate alerts
entries.statement: Analysts spend time opening duplicate alerts individually (up to the first hour of a shift) or have learned to ignore them altogether.

evidence.quote: My analysts spend the first hour of every shift clicking through duplicates.
2 of 5 opened two duplicate PowerShell alerts before realising they were the same.
but we just learned to ignore it.

entries.title: Group duplicate alerts into one row with a count
entries.statement: Users want duplicate alerts grouped into a single row with a count.

evidence.quote: I wish these were one row with a count.
Is there a way to group them?

entries.title: Test runners produce about half of alert volume
entries.statement: According to the PM, test runners account for about half of alert volume.

evidence.quote: test runners are half our alert volume

entries.title: Customers cannot turn off noisy alerts because audit needs them
entries.statement: Duplicate alerts cannot be disabled because they are required for audit, consistent with D-07.

evidence.quote: We can't turn them off, audit needs them.

entries.title: Phishing alerts lack sender and subject
entries.statement: Phishing alerts only say the user clicked a link and do not show the email sender or subject; the customer calls it the most annoying part of the product.

evidence.quote: A phishing alert just says the user clicked a link. It doesn't show the sender or the subject
It's the most annoying part of the product for us.
The phishing alert has no sender address or subject line.

entries.title: Users leave the product to look up phishing details in the mail gateway
entries.statement: For every phishing alert, the security team looks up email details in their mail gateway.

evidence.quote: so every single one I have to go to the mail gateway to understand it.
we have to look everything up in the mail gateway.

entries.title: Add sender and subject to phishing alert details
entries.statement: Customer asks for sender address and subject line in phishing alert details.

evidence.quote: Please add them

entries.title: Acme Logistics gets 20-30 phishing alerts a day
entries.statement: Acme Logistics receives 20-30 phishing email alerts per day.

evidence.quote: Twenty, thirty a day.

entries.title: Acme Logistics is renewing
entries.statement: Acme Logistics is renewing, while flagging email alerts as a problem.

evidence.quote: We're renewing, but the email alerts are a problem.

entries.title: CISO regularly reports security posture to the board
entries.statement: The Northwind Health CISO explains security posture to the board using slide decks; cadence is stated as monthly in one source and weekly posture in another.

evidence.quote: I have a board meeting every month where I have to explain our posture.
the weekly posture I can put in a board deck

entries.title: CISO spends half a day screenshotting the product into slides
entries.statement: The CISO builds board reports by taking screenshots and pasting them into slides, taking half a day.

evidence.quote: Right now I take screenshots from Sentinel and paste them into slides. It takes me half a day.

entries.title: Board-ready posture summary or export
entries.statement: The CISO wants an exportable, plain-language posture summary for the board: what happened, whether important systems are safe, and whether response is getting faster.

evidence.quote: Something I can hand to the board. Plain language. What happened, are our important systems safe, are we getting faster.
Is there an export of the weekly posture I can put in a board deck?

entries.title: Containment stalls when no incident lead is available
entries.statement: Because only leads can isolate, containment waits when a lead is offline or busy: 25 minutes lost at Brightline, night-shift waits at Northwind, and an internal analyst isolated nothing for two weeks.

evidence.quote: When a lead isn't around at night, we wait.
Our lead was offline and we lost 25 minutes.
I isolated nothing in two weeks because the lead was always busy with prod.

entries.title: Disabled Isolate button doesn't explain why
entries.statement: Analysts see the Isolate button greyed out without understanding why; 4 of 5 hovered it but only 1 noticed the tooltip, and it can be read as broken.

evidence.quote: On the incident screen, 4 of 5 hovered the disabled Isolate button; only 1 noticed the tooltip.
Why is it grey? Is it broken?
The isolate button is greyed out for me.

entries.title: Show analysts which lead is on call for containment
entries.statement: Analysts don't know who to ask when containment is needed; customers want the on-call lead shown so analysts can contact them.

evidence.quote: But tell the analyst who is on call so they can ping them.
Who can I ask?

entries.title: Customer accepts the containment lock
entries.statement: Northwind Health's SOC lead understands why containment is restricted to leads, citing their own past incident.

evidence.quote: I get why containment is locked, we had our own incident like that years ago.

entries.title: Let analysts isolate test-tagged assets
entries.statement: An incident lead proposed allowing analysts to isolate assets tagged test without a lead, arguing test assets cannot take production down.

evidence.quote: Proposal: for assets tagged test, analysts should be able to isolate without waiting for a lead. Nothing in test can take production down.

entries.title: Analysts may isolate test assets (Slack decision, not in decision log)
entries.statement: The PM decided in Slack that analysts can isolate test-tagged assets without lead approval, planned for next sprint, and said the decision log would be updated. It has not been.

evidence.quote: Decided: analysts can isolate test assets. I'll update the decision log.

conflicts.summary: D-12 (active) says only incident leads may run containment and forbids enabling the button for analysts or bypassing the API check. On 2026-10-08 the PM decided in Slack that analysts can isolate test-tagged assets, but D-12 has not been updated and has no test-asset exception.
conflicts.question: Is D-12 being amended to let analysts isolate test-tagged assets? If so, who approves the change, how is 'test' tagging verified so a mis-tagged production host can't be isolated, and will the decision log be updated before any work starts?
